app.name: Gmail (Google Gmail API via Google Cloud / Google Auth Platform)

verdict.summary: You can connect your own Gmail account within about half an hour while the app is in Testing mode. To let anyone connect, Google has to verify your app. Composio's default scope https://mail.google.com/ is a restricted scope, which means about 6 weeks of review plus a yearly third-party security assessment if Gmail data is stored on or passes through your server. If you only need sensitive scopes (not restricted ones), review is roughly 3-10 business days.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for Gates 1-2. 1-3 days to prepare for verification (home page, privacy policy, domain checks, demo video). Extra effort for the security assessment if you use restricted scopes.
verdict.approval_wait: Brand check: 2-3 business days. Sensitive scopes: 3-10 business days. Restricted scopes: about 6 weeks plus the security assessment (community reports range from 2 to 8 weeks overall).

gates.name: Testing publishing status (External), you as test user
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Google account through your own OAuth client and Composio auth config.
limits: Google shows its unverified-app screen before the consent screen.
Refresh tokens expire after 7 days in Testing unless you only request name, email and profile scopes. After that the connection has to be re-authorized.
Limit of 100 refresh tokens per Google Account per OAuth client ID.

gates.name: Testing mode with test users (or Internal/Workspace-only use)
gates.unlocks: Users you add as test users can connect. If your users are all in your own Google Workspace organization, internal use is exempt from verification.
limits: Only listed test users can authorize (community source).
Unverified apps that use sensitive or restricted scopes have a 100 new-user cap.
Refresh tokens still expire after 7 days in Testing.
A third-party guide says whitelisted Workspace accounts don't count toward the cap but personal Gmail accounts always do (not confirmed by Google).
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after Gate 1 (add test users on the Audience page)

gates.name: In production + OAuth app verification (brand, sensitive or restricted scope)
gates.unlocks: Any Google user can connect, with no unverified-app screen, no 100-user cap and no 7-day refresh-token expiry.
limits: Restricted scopes (for example https://mail.google.com/) need a yearly security assessment by a Google-approved assessor if data is stored on or sent through a server.
If Google rejects a scope, that scope stops working for your users.
If you go to production without verification, the 100-user cap will eventually run out and Google sign-in will be disabled for your users.
gates.time_to_reach: Brand: 2-3 business days. Sensitive: 3-10 business days. Restricted: about 6 weeks plus the security assessment.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Sign in to the Google Cloud console with the account that will own the app and create a new project for this integration. In the API Library, enable the Gmail API. If you keep Composio's default People/contacts scopes, enable the People API too. Google sends all verification emails to the project owners, so use an owner mailbox someone monitors.
gotchas: Google says each app in a project that uses restricted scopes must be submitted for verification separately. Keep one app per project to keep things simple.

steps.title: Fill in Branding on the Google Auth Platform
steps.detail: Go to Google Auth Platform > Branding and enter the app name, user support email, logo, developer contact email, and the home page, privacy policy and terms of service links. Add the top private domain of those links under Authorized domains.
gotchas: Once the app is external and shows a logo or display name, brand verification is required before that branding appears to users.

steps.title: Set Audience to External / Testing and add test users
steps.detail: On the Audience page, choose user type External (or Internal if only your Workspace organization will use it), leave the publishing status as Testing, and add your own account plus any testers under Test users.
gotchas: In Testing, refresh tokens expire after 7 days, so Composio connections will need re-authorizing every week.
Internal apps skip the unverified flow, but only for accounts in your own domain.

steps.title: Choose the smallest set of scopes on Data Access
steps.detail: List the Gmail features your agent actually uses and map each one to the narrowest scope that covers it. Then add those scopes on the Data Access page. Use https://mail.google.com/ only if you need IMAP/SMTP or permanent deletion, because it triggers restricted-scope verification. Check each scope's tier against Google's Gmail scopes table.
gotchas: Community sources disagree on whether gmail.modify and gmail.readonly are sensitive or restricted. Rely on Google's table.
The scope list in your Composio auth config must match what you register here.

steps.title: Create a Web application OAuth client with the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: On the Clients page, create an OAuth client of type Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. Copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URI must match exactly, including scheme, case and trailing slash. Otherwise you get redirect_uri_mismatch.
It must use HTTPS. Raw IP addresses aren't allowed.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config and test-connect your account
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom auth config for the gmail toolkit using your client ID, client secret and chosen scopes. Then run a test authorization with a test-user account and confirm that a Gmail API call succeeds. Google's authorize endpoint returns invalid_client if the client ID is wrong.
gotchas: Expect the unverified-app screen. Testers have to click through it.

steps.title: Publish the home page and privacy policy
steps.detail: Draft and publish a public home page that describes what the app does and links to the privacy policy and terms of service. Host the privacy policy on the same domain as the home page. It must say how you access, use, store and share Google user data, and include the Google API Services User Data Policy / Limited Use disclosure.
gotchas: The privacy policy has to be linked from the consent screen (Branding page).

steps.title: Verify domain ownership in Google Search Console
steps.detail: Verify every domain used in the home page, privacy policy, terms of service, redirect URIs and JavaScript origins in Google Search Console, using an account that is an owner or editor on the project.
gotchas: Your redirect URI points at Composio's domain, which you can't verify. See Blockers.

steps.title: Write scope justifications and record a demo video
steps.detail: Draft a one-paragraph justification for each sensitive or restricted scope. Then record a screen video showing the OAuth consent flow and how the app uses each requested scope, and upload it to YouTube as unlisted. An agent can draft the text and script, but you record the video.

steps.title: Switch to In production and submit for verification
steps.detail: On the Audience page, click Publish app to set the status to In production. Run Verify Branding, then submit the app for verification with your justifications and video link.
gotchas: Being In production without verification still shows the unverified screen and keeps the 100-user cap.

steps.title: Wait for Google's review and answer its emails
steps.detail: Google's published estimates are 2-3 business days for brand verification, about 10 business days for sensitive scopes (another Google page says 3-5 working days), and about 6 weeks for restricted scopes. Reviewers contact project owners by email, so reply quickly to avoid delays.

steps.title: Complete the security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: If you use restricted scopes and Gmail data is stored on or sent through your server (including through Composio), hire a Google-empanelled assessor for the security assessment and repeat it every year. A community source estimates roughly $540-$1k per year for a CASA Tier 2 assessment through self-serve labs.

steps.title: If you call Google Workspace MCP servers, use an agentic OAuth client
steps.detail: From November 11, 2026, Google Workspace MCP servers (including the Gmail MCP server, currently in Developer Preview) reject OAuth clients that aren't marked as agentic. If your agent uses MCP, create a new OAuth client marked as agentic. A third-party source says apps that only call the Gmail REST API (as Composio's tools do) aren't affected.

requirements.item: Publicly accessible home page describing the app, linking to privacy policy and terms
requirements.detail: Required for every production OAuth app.

requirements.item: Privacy policy on the same domain as the home page, with Limited Use disclosure
requirements.detail: Linked from the consent screen. Must explain how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared.

requirements.item: Domain ownership verified in Google Search Console
requirements.detail: Covers every domain in the home page, privacy policy, terms of service, redirect URIs and JavaScript origins.

requirements.item: Complete Branding: app name, logo, support and developer contact, authorized domains
requirements.detail: Brand verification is needed for external apps that show a name or logo on the consent screen.

requirements.item: Scope justifications and a demo video
requirements.detail: Explain each sensitive or restricted scope and show it in use in an unlisted YouTube video.
Only needed for restricted scopes whose data is stored on or sent through a server.

requirements.item: Exact-match HTTPS redirect URI on a domain you own
requirements.detail: Redirect URIs must match exactly and use HTTPS. Google's policy says they should be on domains you own or are licensed to use.

scopes.effect: Full Gmail access, required for IMAP/SMTP. Triggers restricted-scope verification (about 6 weeks) plus the yearly security assessment when data passes through a server. It is in Composio's default scope set.
Listed as restricted by third-party guides, so it goes through the restricted review path. Confirm in Google's table.
Sources conflict. Some call it sensitive (it can't permanently delete mail), others call it restricted. Check Google's table before you rely on it to avoid the security assessment.
Sensitive-scope verification (about 3-10 business days). No security assessment.
If these are your only scopes, Testing-mode refresh tokens don't expire after 7 days.

scopes.scope: contacts.readonly, contacts.other.readonly, user.*.read (People API scopes in Composio defaults)
scopes.effect: The findings don't give a tier for these. Drop any you don't need. Each sensitive or restricted scope adds to the verification work.

blockers.cause: The redirect URI sent doesn't exactly match one registered on the OAuth client (scheme, case or trailing slash).
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from your Composio auth config into the client's Authorized redirect URIs character for character.

blockers.symptom: Connections break about every 7 days with invalid_grant / expired token
blockers.cause: External apps in Testing status get refresh tokens that expire after 7 days.
blockers.fix: Move the app to In production (and verify it) or use Internal user type. Until then, re-authorize every week.

blockers.symptom: New users can't sign in; Google sign-in disabled
blockers.cause: An unverified app using sensitive or restricted scopes has used up its 100 new-user cap.
blockers.fix: Submit for verification before onboarding real users.

blockers.symptom: Verification stalls on domain ownership for the redirect URI
blockers.cause: Google verifies every domain tied to your redirect URIs, and the Composio callback is on Composio's domain, which you can't verify in Search Console.
blockers.fix: Ask Composio whether it supports a custom or white-labeled redirect domain you own, or how its customers get Gmail verification approved with its callback URL.

blockers.symptom: Restricted-scope verification blocked pending security assessment
blockers.cause: Restricted Gmail data is stored on or sent through a server (yours or Composio's).
blockers.fix: Use sensitive-only scopes if your features allow it. Otherwise book a Google-empanelled assessor early and budget for yearly reassessment.

blockers.symptom: Google Workspace MCP server rejects requests after Nov 11, 2026
blockers.cause: The OAuth client isn't marked as agentic.
blockers.fix: Create a new OAuth client marked as agentic and switch to it.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Gmail OAuth for prototyping. It requires no Google Cloud setup. Its default scopes include the restricted https://mail.google.com/, and its verification status and user cap couldn't be confirmed. Register your own Google Cloud client when you need your own branding on the consent screen, a smaller scope set (for example sensitive-only, to avoid restricted review), or your own verified app for production. With your own client, paste Composio's callback URL as the redirect URI. Expect domain verification questions, because that callback is on Composio's domain.

open_questions: The official Google sensitive/restricted scope table wasn't fetched. Sources disagree on gmail.modify, gmail.readonly and the settings scopes. Confirm each scope on Google's Gmail scopes page.
Tiers for Composio's default People API scopes (contacts.readonly, user.birthday.read, etc.) weren't researched.
Can a self-registered client pass domain verification while its redirect URI is Composio's backend.composio.dev callback? Does Composio offer a custom redirect domain?
Whether Composio's managed Gmail client is verified, and what user cap it has, couldn't be determined.
Google's timelines conflict: sensitive is 3-5 working days on one page and 10 business days on another. CASA cost and yearly terms come only from third-party sources.
The console path (Google Auth Platform > Branding / Audience / Data Access / Clients) is drawn from Google guides and release-note text. The console itself wasn't checked.
A reported 2026 Gmail API quota cut to 6,000 units per user per minute comes from one third-party source. Check it on Google's usage-limits page.
